title: Drift Regimes Factor: regime-conditioned value+reversal on S&P500 (new research round concept)
rationale: arXiv:2511.12490 ('Discovery of a 13-Sharpe OOS Factor: Drift Regimes') identifies a regime-conditioned long-short equity factor combining value (70%) and short-term reversal (30%) signals, activated ONLY during stock-specific 'drift regimes' (>60% positive days in trailing 63-day window). OOS Sharpe 13.19 over 20-year S&P500 (2004-2024) with 0.6bp transaction costs. Degrades to Sharpe 6.3 with 10bp costs. Key mechanism: value+reversal are already known alpha sources, but their alpha is highly regime-dependent. Trading them ONLY when the specific stock is in a positive drift regime removes the noise and concentrates alpha. Implementation is straightforward: (1) compute UpFraction_i,t = fraction of positive-return days in trailing 63d, (2) compute BASE = 0.7*value_pctile + 0.3*(-10d_return z-score), (3) EDGE = BASE * I(UpFraction > 0.60), (4) long top decile EDGE, short bottom decile. Value metric used: inverse stock price percentile (not P/B or P/E — purely price level). This approach has near-zero factor exposure (R-squared < 3% to standard factors). The drift regime filter concept is also applicable as a PEAD amplifier: apply it as a veto on PEAD gap positions for stocks NOT in drift regime on earnings day.
content:
### Drift Regimes Factor: regime-gated value+reversal for concentrated alpha
- LESSON: Value and short-term reversal signals are highly regime-dependent. Trading them ONLY when the stock is in a 'drift regime' (>60% positive-return days in trailing 63-day window) achieves Sharpe 13.19 OOS on S&P500 2004-2024 with 0.6bp costs (Sharpe 6.3 at 10bp). EDGE_i,t = (0.7*value_pctile + 0.3*(-10d_return z-score)) * I(UpFraction_i,t > 0.60). The regime gate is the key innovation — it removes the same signals when the stock is in a choppy/neutral phase.
- LESSON: The value metric in the original paper is 'inverse stock price percentile' (not P/B or P/E). Simple, low-information-cost proxy. R-squared to standard factors < 3%, meaning alpha is genuinely incremental.
- LESSON: The drift regime filter (UpFraction > 0.60 over 63 days) is a useful MODIFIER for existing signals, not just this factor. Consider applying it to PEAD gap signals: require that the stock was in a drift regime in the 63 days preceding earnings day as an additional quality filter (stocks already trending up are more likely to sustain a positive gap).
- WHEN: Designing a new long-short equity factor round (candidate R33 or R34). Also consider drift regime as an optional filter overlay on R28 PEAD signals.
- SOURCE: arXiv:2511.12490 (Nov 2025) — 'Discovery of a 13-Sharpe OOS Factor: Drift Regimes'. Walk-forward validated, frozen parameters, 20-year S&P500.
